title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics and parity across Python/TypeScript/Go (v1.66.0)
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: bring parity and ergonomics improvements for auth, retry middleware, and streaming APIs across the three official SDKs (Python, TypeScript, Go). Customers reported inconsistent behavior between SDKs for token refresh, streaming backpressure, and retry metadata propagation which made cross-language integrations fragile. This PR consolidates the auth surface (AuthCredentials interface), standardizes the retry middleware semantics (idempotency keys, retryable codes, and jittered exponential backoff), and aligns streaming ergonomics (async iterators in Python/TS, channel-based streaming helpers in Go). Changes include: - unified AuthCredentials abstraction and default token refresher implementation - retry middleware implemented with common policy config and automatic header propagation - streaming client helpers: Python async generator, TypeScript AsyncIterable, Go StreamConn with controlled prefetch/backpressure - ergonomics improvements: context managers in Python, safe async iterator closing in TS, explicit Close/Cancel semantics in Go - parity fixes and small behavior changes to match hosted API semantics and ensure equivalent error wrapping and codes across SDKs - version bumps: python v1.66.0, typescript v1.66.0, go v1.66.0 See migration notes and release notes below. Checklist: - [x] implement shared auth/retry contracts - [x] implement streaming ergonomics and helpers in each SDK - [x] add unit and integration tests for retry propagation and streaming cancellation - [x] update changelogs and bump package versions - [x] run cross-SDK interoperability smoke tests - [x] docs snippet updates (examples) Migration notes: - Auth: replace custom token handling with AuthCredentials class/struct in each SDK. Backwards compatible adapter provided for existing token callbacks. - Retries: default behavior is unchanged (same number of attempts) but header propagation and idempotency key handling are standardized; rare edge cases where custom retry hooks relied on non-propagated headers may need adjusting. - Streaming: consumers should adopt the new helpers for proper cancellation handling; raw sockets are still available but require manual cleanup. Related linear items: ENG-4821 (auth unification), ENG-4890 (streaming ergonomics), ENG-4912 (sdk parity test harness). Related PRs/changes: examples and docs updates in redwood-examples and redwood-docs will follow in separate PRs.
